questions.q: Put a name to the first of the five solution-design stages.
options: Evaluate options against constraints
Decide and document
Clarify the requirement
Validate before building
questions.explain: The process starts by clarifying the requirement itself — confirming it's the real need, not a misunderstood or premature restatement of one — before any design work begins.

questions.q: What does "exploring the solution space" mean in stage two of the process?
options: Immediately building a prototype in a sandbox
Listing the realistic alternative ways a requirement could be met, without settling on one yet
Asking the stakeholder to pick a solution themselves
Searching Trailhead for a matching badge
questions.explain: Stage two deliberately resists settling on an answer — it's about surfacing the real set of viable alternatives (a formula field, automation, a scheduled job, an upstream change, etc.) before any of them gets evaluated or chosen.

questions.q: What is the single most common failure this lesson identifies in solution design?
options: Spending too much time documenting decisions
Validating a design with stakeholders too early
Collapsing straight from requirement to a chosen build, with no options ever considered or recorded
Using too many diagrams during design reviews
questions.explain: Jumping straight from the requirement to a single chosen implementation, without ever considering or documenting alternatives, means there's no way to tell afterward whether the result was actually the best option or just the first one anyone thought of.

questions.q: Why does stage five ("validate before building") happen before implementation rather than after?
options: Because Salesforce requires a formal sign-off before any deployment
Because catching a misunderstanding before the build costs a conversation, while catching it after costs a rebuild
Because developers are not allowed to see requirements directly
It doesn't matter when validation happens, as long as it happens eventually
questions.explain: Validating the design against the original requesters before real implementation time is spent is far cheaper than discovering a misunderstanding after a developer has already built the wrong thing.

questions.q: How does the five-stage process change between a one-field tweak and a multi-system migration, per this lesson?
options: The stages themselves are skipped for small changes
A completely different process is used for large initiatives
The stages stay the same; only the amount of ceremony and documentation scales with what's at stake
Only large initiatives require clarifying the requirement at all
questions.explain: Clarify, explore, evaluate, decide, validate applies at any scale — a ten-minute change might run through it informally in someone's head, while a multi-week initiative might formalize each stage with documents and sign-offs, but the underlying sequence doesn't change shape.
